title: Your right to personal liberty
summary: You are entitled to your personal liberty. You cannot be deprived of your freedom except in the specific cases and by the lawful procedure the Constitution allows.
body_plain: The Constitution says every person is entitled to their personal liberty, and no one may be deprived of it except in the situations the law clearly allows - such as being arrested on reasonable suspicion of an offence, and only through a procedure permitted by law. This is the foundation of the other rights around arrest, detention and bail: freedom is the rule, and any detention must justify itself under the law.
rights: You can only be detained in the specific cases the law allows, and only by lawful procedure.
If you are detained, you keep your rights to know why, to remain silent, and to a lawyer.
do_list: Ask whether you are under arrest or free to go.
If detained, calmly ask on what legal grounds.
Keep a record of what happened and who was involved.
dont_list: Do not resist physically, even if the detention feels unlawful.
Do not assume you must go along with any request just because it comes from an officer.
common_situations: You are blocked from leaving a place by officials or private actors.
You are taken to a station 'to answer questions' but are not told whether you can leave.
Someone is held because the police want a relative or associate to report.
words_to_use: Am I being detained, or am I free to leave?
What lawful reason are you relying on to restrict my liberty?
Please let me contact my lawyer or another person of my choice.
if_violated: Record when freedom of movement was first restricted, every place you were held, and when release occurred.
Preserve messages, call records, witness details, transport information, and any custody or release document.
Seek prompt legal advice about release, compensation, apology, or other enforcement remedies.

citations.source_name: 1999 Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria
